# Quick repo context

- This repository holds vendor-proprietary artifacts for several Samsung device trees: `corsica`, `ivory`, `nevisp`, `vivalto`, `zanin`, and shared `rhea-common` files.
- Each device directory contains: `BoardConfigVendor.mk`, `<device>-vendor-blobs.mk`, `<device>-vendor.mk` and a `proprietary/` tree with `bin/`, `etc/`, `lib/`, `usr/`, and other blob locations.

# What matters (big picture)

- These are prebuilt vendor blobs used by an Android build system (AOSP/Lineage/CyanogenMod-era). The repo is organized by device; each device exports prebuilt packages via generated `Android.mk` and vendor makefiles.
- Example: `rhea-common/Android.mk` (generated by `device/samsung/rhea-common/setup-makefiles.sh`) lists many prebuilt APKs using `LOCAL_SRC_FILES := proprietary/app/...` and `include $(BUILD_PREBUILT)`.

# Project-specific patterns and conventions

- Do not assume source code for blobs — treat most files in `proprietary/` as opaque binaries; changes are usually about listing/remapping them in vendor makefiles rather than recompiling.
- `*-vendor-blobs.mk` files and `setup-makefiles.sh` are the canonical sources for which blobs are packaged. `Android.mk` files under `*-common` are often generated; prefer editing the generator or the `*-vendor-blobs.mk` over hand-editing generated `Android.mk` files.
- Hardware modules and HALs live in `proprietary/lib/` and `proprietary/lib/hw/`. When tracing an issue, check for `*.so` blobs referenced by BoardConfig or vendor makefiles.

# Integration points & where to look

- Device/device-common files: `rhea-common/Android.mk` (prebuilt apps example).
- Device folders: `corsica/`, `ivory/`, `nevisp/`, `vivalto/`, `zanin/` — each includes `.mk` files and `proprietary/` blobs.
- Board-level configs: `BoardConfigVendor.mk` and `*-vendor.mk` — these influence build flags and which blobs are packaged.

# Typical developer workflow (assumptions)

NOTE: this repo supplies vendor blobs for an Android build tree. I assume you use a standard AOSP/Lineage build environment. Please confirm your exact build target/names. Typical local flow:

```bash
# from AOSP/Lineage root (example)
source build/envsetup.sh
# pick the device build target (confirm exact name for these devices)
lunch <vendor_device>-userdebug
# build vendor artifacts (may be `mka vendor` or `make vendor` depending on setup)
mka vendor
```

If you have custom scripts or CI steps that assemble or push blobs into the AOSP tree, point to them so the instructions can be extended.

# How to change / add blobs

- Add new files under the appropriate `proprietary/` directory and add entries to the device `*-vendor-blobs.mk` or the `setup-makefiles.sh` generator so the generated `Android.mk` picks them up. Avoid manual edits to generated files.
- To find references to prebuilt APKs or binaries, search for `proprietary/app/` or `LOCAL_SRC_FILES :=` in the repo.

# Examples of useful searches

- Find prebuilt packages: `git grep "proprietary/app/" -n`
- Find generated makefiles: `git grep "generated by" -n` (some headers include generator hints, e.g., `setup-makefiles.sh`).

# What AI agents should not do

- Do not attempt to re-implement or modify binary blob internals — treat them as opaque unless the repository contains corresponding source.
- Avoid committing large new binary files without maintainers’ guidance; prefer adding or editing makefile entries and verifying packaging steps.
